projects.title: Code Buddy
projects.tags: Multi-agent systems · LLM tooling · Developer experience
bullets: Connected change events to a review pipeline that retrieves code context, detects issues, generates candidate fixes, and validates the result before delivery.
Built dependency-aware retrieval using Tree-sitter, symbol indexes, and cached lookups so reviewers could inspect definitions and call relationships beyond the changed lines.
Compared agent findings against labeled code changes using precision and recall, giving prompt and model updates a repeatable evaluation process.
projects.headline: From a pilot to 12,000 engineers.
projects.summary: A code-review platform I architected at Qualcomm, connecting issue detection, candidate fixes, and validation for 12,000+ engineers across 4,000+ repositories.

bullets: Processed MediaPipe face and hand landmarks in the browser to estimate eye closure, blink activity, head movement, and recognized gestures.

projects.title: HealthSense
projects.tags: Foundation Model, Wearable AI, PyTorch · SparQ Qualcomm TechFest 2026
bullets: Connected five signal types to preprocessing, task-specific outputs, and a common dashboard for inspecting the analysis.
Built a compact 1D ECG CNN in PyTorch with training and ONNX export scripts, plus runtime provider selection with a CPU fallback.
Tested ECG classification on a small, four-record PhysioNet sample. The experiment used window-level splits; it does not establish performance on unseen patients. BioTrain adaptation is simulated.
projects.headline: Exploring intelligence for wearable signals.
projects.summary: An experimental biosignal dashboard combining ECG classification, signal-processing heuristics, and explanations across five sensor streams.

posts.title: The Voice Agent Problem Nobody Talks About
posts.excerpt: When you talk to a voice agent, the hard part is not transcription or synthesis. The hard part is what happens when you interrupt it mid-sentence, or pause to think and then keep talking, or when two people speak at once. Real conversations are messy. They have false starts, interruptions, and moments where you change your mind halfway through a sentence.

posts.title: How Claude Learned to Watch Videos: The Decomposition Pattern for Multimodal AI Agents
posts.excerpt: Claude can read a webpage. It can run a script. It can browse a repository. What it cannot do, out of the box, is watch a video. You paste a YouTube link and it has to either guess from the title or pull a transcript that is missing 90% of what is on screen.

posts.title: Building Code Buddy: A Multi-Agent GenAI Code Review Platform at Qualcomm
posts.excerpt: At Qualcomm, I had the opportunity to architect Code Buddy , a multi-agent GenAI code-review platform that's now deployed across 4,000+ repositories and serves 12,000+ engineers. Here's the story of how we built it, the architecture decisions that mattered, and what we learned along the way.
